title: Drills over music
intro: One pair, “el atasco” — “traffic jam”, in every structure, over one bed (bright-organic), so only the structure changes. The native voice (Kore) says Spanish; the guide (Charon) says English. Each clip opens and closes with a bar of music. The grid under each clip shows what starts on each eighth note.

cards.title: Classic retrieval drill
cards.why: Word, a silent bar to recall the meaning, the meaning; then the pair twice more; then a rest. Production takes 0–2 per line, as a loop renders them.
cards.facts: 80 BPM · bar 3.00 s · 8 bars + 1 in + 1 out · bed bright-organic

groups.title: Two or four
groups.intro: The pair two or four times, in different rhythms, filling four bars.

cards.title: Pair per bar
cards.why: The word on beat 1, its translation on beat 3, four bars running: no gaps, one steady pulse. The densest version of today's drill that still leaves each line room.
cards.facts: 80 BPM · bar 3.00 s · 4 bars + 1 in + 1 out · bed bright-organic

cards.title: Word, a bar of silence, then pairs
cards.why: The word alone, then a whole empty bar for the meaning to surface before it is given, then two tight pairs. Retrieval first, reinforcement after.

cards.title: Doubles
cards.why: Word twice, translation twice, twice over. Repetition in pairs is how a chorus is built; it gives the ear a second chance at each line before it changes.

cards.title: A bar each
cards.why: Today's rhythm, one line to a bar, without the retrieval gap: four bars, two pairs. Spacious, the easiest to follow while doing something else.

cards.title: Four on the beat

groups.title: Echo
groups.intro: Repeat after me: a cue and a silent bar to say the word in.

cards.title: Echo, cued by the guide in English
cards.why: Repeat after me. The word, the guide's “your turn”, a bar of silence to say it in, then the word again to check against. Saying it aloud is production, and the second hearing corrects it.

cards.title: Echo, cued in the target language

cards.title: Echo with no cue, only the music

groups.title: Slow, normal, fast
groups.intro: Three speeds of one word, by stretching, by asking, or both.

cards.title: Speeds by stretching one recording
cards.why: The word three times, slow enough to hear every sound, then natural, then quick, and the translation after. Slow is for the ear; fast is how it is really said. Here one recording is stretched to 0.8×, 1.0× and 1.3× (formant-preserving): identical delivery, only the speed changes.
cards.notes: Take lengths before fitting: W el atasco (×0.8): 1.03 s; W el atasco: 0.82 s; W el atasco (×1.3): 0.63 s; T traffic jam: 1.10 s.
cards.facts: 80 BPM · bar 3.00 s · 4 bars + 1 in + 1 out · bed bright-organic

cards.title: Speeds by asking the voice
cards.why: The word three times, slow enough to hear every sound, then natural, then quick, and the translation after. Slow is for the ear; fast is how it is really said. Here the voice is asked for each speed in words, with nothing stretched. A bare note is used, since production's pace words would contradict it.
cards.notes: Take lengths before fitting: W el atasco (slowly): 2.98 s; W el atasco (naturally): 0.87 s; W el atasco (quickly and crisply): 0.70 s; T traffic jam: 1.10 s.
cards.facts: 80 BPM · bar 3.00 s · 4 bars + 1 in + 1 out · bed bright-organic

cards.title: Asked, then nudged by stretching
cards.why: The word three times, slow enough to hear every sound, then natural, then quick, and the translation after. Slow is for the ear; fast is how it is really said. The voice is asked for each speed, and the stretch finishes the fast one (1.15×). The slow one is left alone: asked for, it is already 3.4× the natural length.
cards.notes: Take lengths before fitting: W el atasco (slowly): 2.98 s; W el atasco (naturally): 0.87 s; W el atasco (×1.15; quickly and crisply): 0.61 s; T traffic jam: 1.10 s.

groups.title: Chant
groups.intro: The word's syllables on eighth notes, then the whole word.

cards.title: Chant on eighths, one take cut and snapped: el-a-tas-co
cards.why: The voice chants the word once. The take is cut at its loudness dips into 4 syllables, and each is placed on an eighth note, with the stressed one louder, then the whole word and its meaning. The rhythm is the grid's, not the voice's.
cards.notes: The chanted take was 2.6 s, stretched ×1.96 before cutting.
cards.facts: 80 BPM · bar 3.00 s · 4 bars + 1 in + 1 out · bed bright-organic
